Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

complex adjective

intricate, complicated

also complicated, intricate, involved, not simple, complexity, complication, intricacy

classical

Cic. Fin. 3.3: nec … quicquam implicātum aut tortuōsum (Lewis & Short, s.v. implicō)
Cic. de Or. 3.52 (Lewis & Short)

implicātus, implicāta, implicātum

adjective, declension

entangled, intricate, complicated

Literally “folded in, entwined”; of a question, a speech or an affair, complicated. Gellius has implicātissima quaestiō.

Other words

  • involūtus, involūta, involūtum — involved, intricate, obscure

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 102: rēs involūtās dēfīniendō explicāre (Lewis & Short, s.v. involvō)

    Literally “wrapped up”: complicated because hidden, hard to make out.

  • perplexus, perplexa, perplexum — tangled, intricate, confusing

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Liv. 35.14: perplexum Pūnicō astū respōnsum (Lewis & Short)

    Not in Cicero or Caesar; Livy uses it of obscure, ambiguous words (Lewis & Short). It does not mean “perplexed” of a person.

  • multiplex, multiplicis — with many parts, manifold

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.136: alvus est multiplex et tortuōsa (Lewis & Short)

    Complex in the sense of made of many folds or parts; also “many times as great”.

  • implicātiō, implicātiōnis f. — entanglement, complexity

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.139: nervōrum implicātiō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sest. 99: propter implicātiōnem reī familiāris (Lewis & Short)

    The noun of implicāre: an interweaving, and so the complexity or tangle of an affair. For “the complexity of the question”, Latin also says quam implicāta sit quaestiō.

Examples

  • nec in Torquātī sermōne quicquam implicātum aut tortuōsum fuit

    and in what Torquatus said there was nothing complicated or twistedCic. Fin. 3.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • perplexum Pūnicō astū respōnsum

    an answer made intricate with Carthaginian cunningLiv. 35.14 (Lewis & Short)

  • Rēs implicātior est quam putābam.

    It’s more complicated than I thought.composed

See also structure.
